network.overall_strategy: The network is built around the experimentally supported surface cyanosulfidic sequence of Patel et al. (2015), which converts 3-aminopropanal into proline through cyanohydrin formation, H2S-driven thiolation/cyclization, Cu/H2S reductive deoxygenation, thione-to-nitrile conversion, and nitrile hydrolysis. To provide 10 distinct pathways without inventing an unsupported chiral-resolution step, the graph varies only chemically plausible upstream entries into the 3-aminopropanal/acrolein pool and two terminal hydrolysis regimes. Thus five entry modes converge on the same pyrrolidine-building core, and each is paired with either ambient or geothermal-accelerated nitrile hydrolysis. The requested target is L-proline, but the provided literature supports only constitutional/racemic proline; no separate prebiotic enantioselective step is added.

reactions.name: Acrolein ammoniation to 3-aminopropanal

conditions.other: Anoxic ammoniacal pool or shoreline film; rapid trapping is needed because beta-amino aldehydes are reactive.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia performs aza-Michael addition to acrolein, followed by proton transfer and tautomerization to the beta-amino aldehyde 3-aminopropanal.
reactions.reasoning: The review identifies 3-aminopropanal as a plausible prebiotic product of acrolein plus NH3 and explicitly mentions Michael-type ammoniation as an entry into the proline network. This feeder is chemically reasonable in surface pools, but the low steady-state stability of 3-aminopropanal remains a significant limitation (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Glycerol dehydration to acrolein

conditions.other: Hot acidic dry-down on a geothermal apron or evaporitic shoreline; two water equivalents are inferred.

reactions.mechanism: Heating drives sequential dehydration of glycerol to the conjugated aldehyde acrolein under low-water-activity conditions.
reactions.reasoning: The literature review notes thermal decomposition/dehydration of glycerol as a plausible prebiotic source of acrolein. This branch is therefore chemically plausible but not part of the experimentally demonstrated proline sequence itself; it requires hotter, drier, and likely more acidic surface microenvironments than the Patel core, and side reactions such as charring or polymerization are expected (Patel et al., 2015; speculative feeder).

reactions.name: 3-Hydroxypropanal dehydration to acrolein

conditions.other: Acidic hot-spring or evaporative dry-down setting with low water activity.

reactions.mechanism: Thermal elimination of water from 3-hydroxypropanal furnishes the alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde acrolein.
reactions.reasoning: This feeder is speculative because no direct support for it appears in the provided report. It is included on chemical merit: dehydration of a hydroxy aldehyde to acrolein is a conservative C3 entry into the same aminoaldehyde/cyanosulfidic core used downstream. The uncertainty lies in the availability of 3-hydroxypropanal and competition from hydration, oligomerization, and rearrangement (speculative; no direct experimental support in the provided review).

reactions.name: Sulfidic reductive amination of malondialdehyde to 3-aminopropanal

conditions.other: Anoxic sulfidic pool; selective mono-reductive amination is required despite the high reactivity of the dialdehyde.

reactions.mechanism: One aldehyde of malondialdehyde forms an imine with ammonia, which is then reduced under sulfidic conditions to the aminoaldehyde; sulfur is tracked as the formal oxidation sink and water as the condensation product.
reactions.reasoning: The review explicitly mentions reductive amination of malondialdehyde as a possible source of 3-aminopropanal, but no selective prebiotic conversion is demonstrated. This node is therefore deliberately marked speculative and written as the minimal atom-balanced sulfidic net transformation needed to connect that suggestion to the Patel core. Malondialdehyde instability and overreaction are major concerns (Patel et al., 2015; speculative feeder).

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin formation from 3-aminopropanal

conditions.other: Anoxic cyanosulfidic shallow pool with dissolved HCN.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide adds nucleophilically to the aldehyde carbonyl of 3-aminopropanal to form the alpha-hydroxynitrile 4-amino-2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This is one of the experimentally demonstrated steps in the proline sequence. It is the key C-C bond-forming extension from a C3 aminoaldehyde to the C4 aminonitrile required for later ring closure (Patel et al., 2015). The chief practical limitation remains the availability and preservation of 3-aminopropanal noted in the review.

reactions.name: H2S-mediated thiolation and cyclization to 3-hydroxypyrrolidine-2-thione
reactions.mechanism: H2S converts the nitrile into a thioamide equivalent, after which the terminal amine attacks intramolecularly to close the five-membered ring and expel ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) experimentally support this one-pot thiolation/cyclization. It is the decisive ring-forming step that makes proline accessible: the 3-aminopropanal-derived chain length is exactly suited for five-membered pyrrolidine closure, which explains the route's structural selectivity.

reactions.name: Cu/H2S reductive deoxygenation to pyrrolidine-2-thione

conditions.other: Aqueous sulfidic surface setting with dispersed Cu0; sulfur bookkeeping is represented as elemental sulfur.

reactions.mechanism: The Cu/H2S reducing system removes the C3 hydroxyl group as water, yielding the fully reduced pyrrolidine-2-thione; sulfur is tracked as the formal oxidation sink.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) demonstrated the deoxygenation using a Cu/H2S system. In this graph, H2S is written explicitly as the reductant and sulfur as the atom-balanced oxidation sink because the exact sulfur speciation is not resolved in a coefficient-free node representation. The review correctly notes that the abundance and persistence of native Cu0 are open questions in prebiotic settings.

reactions.name: Thione-to-nitrile conversion to pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile

conditions.other: HCN-rich cyanosulfidic pool; sulfur is recorded as a neutral sulfur sink for explicit atom balance.

reactions.mechanism: HCN converts the C2 thione/thioamide functionality of the pyrrolidine ring into the corresponding nitrile-bearing carbon center, with sulfur extrusion.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support conversion of pyrrolidine-2-thione into pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile as part of the proline sequence. The paper discusses sulfur recycling within the cyanosulfidic network; here the coproduct is tracked as elemental sulfur rather than H2S so the graph remains explicitly atom-balanced without hidden proton/electron carriers. This is a bookkeeping choice rather than a rejection of the sulfur-cycle concept (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Ambient aqueous nitrile hydrolysis to proline

conditions.other: Long aqueous residence time in shallow pools; two water equivalents are inferred.

reactions.mechanism: Net sequential hydration of the nitrile to an amide and then to the carboxylic acid gives proline with release of ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: This hydrolysis endpoint is part of the Patel et al. (2015) proline sequence. The node is written as a net hydrolysis, with the amide stage left implicit, and it should be interpreted as producing constitutional proline rather than a demonstrated enantioenriched L-product. The review identifies slow ambient nitrile hydrolysis as a real kinetic bottleneck (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Geothermal-accelerated nitrile hydrolysis to proline

conditions.other: Warm geothermal pool with evaporation-concentration and pH cycling; same net stoichiometry as rxn_009.

reactions.mechanism: The same nitrile-to-acid hydrolysis occurs as in rxn_009, but heating and concentration are invoked to accelerate the otherwise slow hydration/hydrolysis sequence.
reactions.reasoning: This is a condition-variant of the same terminal hydrolysis, included because the review specifically highlights nitrile hydrolysis as a bottleneck and suggests that temperature and changing solution chemistry could improve rates. The endpoint is consistent with Patel et al. (2015), but the acceleration under geothermal cycling is only chemically motivated, not directly demonstrated for the proline system in the provided literature; as above, no enantioselection is established.

Main concerns are that mol_005 is used as an entry intermediate rather than a declared starting feedstock, rxn_007 needs explicit Cu0/H2S surface conditions, rxn_008 is drawn with elemental sulfur instead of the literature sulfur recycle, and ambient nitrile hydrolysis is slow. The route reaches constitutional or racemic proline, not demonstrated L-proline.

Revise rxn_008 to give H2S or justify why sulfur is isolated as elemental S under the stated conditions.

evaluation.network_feedback: Network validity is high: the graph is connected, molecule IDs are consistent, and the RDKit check reports no unbalanceable reactions. Literature alignment is strong for the Patel et al. core sequence rxn_005-rxn_010, but only moderate for the upstream supply steps rxn_001-rxn_004. Confidence is reduced because rxn_007 relies on Cu0/H2S reduction without explicit Cu0 in the formal graph, rxn_008 uses elemental sulfur rather than the literature-style sulfur recycle or H2S release, and rxn_002, rxn_009, and rxn_010 need explicit stoichiometric coefficients (mol_012 -> mol_011 + 2 mol_003; mol_009 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_010 + mol_004). The network achieves proline constitutionally and likely racemically, not a demonstrated L-proline product. P2 is the strongest chemistry-wise once 3-aminopropanal is granted; among declared starting-node routes, P8 is the least problematic. Overall this is a good constitutional proline network, but it does not meet the 0.9 approval threshold for an approved L-proline network.
